text:
A ball is thrown upward with an initial velocity
$V_{0}$ from the surface of the earth. The motion
of the ball is affected by a drag force equal to
m$γu^{2} ($where m is mass of the ball, u is its
instantaneous velocity and $γ$ is a constant).
Time taken by the ball to rise to its zenith is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, drag force, $F=mγv^{2}$ ......(i)

As we know, general equation of force

$=ma$ .........(ii)

Comparing Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$a=γv^{2}$

The net retardation of the ball when thrown vertically upward is therefore 

$a_{\text{net}}=-(g+γv^{2})=\frac{dv}{dt}$, where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

Rearranging terms gives us :

$\frac{dv}{g+γv^{2}}=-dt$

We now need to integrate both sides of this equation.

When the ball is thrown upward with velocity $v_{0}$ and reaches its zenith ( "zenith" refers to the highest point that the ball reaches in its upward trajectory.), the velocity is $0$. The time to reach the zenith is $t$.

So the integral equation is :

$\int\limits _{v_{0}}^{0}\frac{dv}{γv^{2}+g}=-\int\limits _{0}^{t}dt$

Separating the constants from the integral :

$\frac{1}{γ}\int\limits _{v_{0}}^{0}\frac{1}{\left (\frac{g}{γ}+v^{2}\right )}dv=-\int\limits _{0}^{t}dt$

Recognizing the integral as the standard form $\frac{1}{x^{2}+a^{2}}=\frac{1}{a}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )$, we write the integral in terms of the arctangent function.

This gives us :

$\frac{1}{γ}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{g}{γ}}}\right )\left [\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{v}{\sqrt{\frac{g}{γ}}}\right )\right ]_{v_{0}}^{0}=-t$

Evaluating the integral at the bounds gives us :

$\frac{1}{\sqrt{γg}}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{γ}v_{0}}{\sqrt{g}}\right )=t$

Therefore, the time taken by the ball to rise to its zenith, considering the drag force, is given by 

$t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{γg}}\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{\frac{γ}{g}}V_{0}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text:
Two wires A & B are carrying currents $I_{1}$ & $I_{2}$
as shown in the figure. The separation between
them is d. A third wire C carrying a current I
is to be kept parallel to them at a distance x from
A such that the net force acting on it is zero.
The possible values of x are :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Net force on wire carrying current I per unit
length is

$\frac{μ_{0}I_{1}I}{2πx}+\frac{μ_{0}I_{2}I}{2π(d-x)}=0$

$\frac{I_{1}}{x}=\frac{I_{2}}{x-d}$

$\Rightarrow x=\frac{I_{1}d}{I_{1}-I_{2}}$

text:
A transformer consisting of 300 turns in the
primary and 150 turns in the secondary gives
output power of 2.2 kW. If the current in the
secondary coil is 10A, then the input voltage
and current in the primary coil are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $N_{P} = 300, N_{s} = 150, P_{0} = 2200W$

$I_{s} = 10 A$

$P_{0} = V_{0}I_{0}$ $\Rightarrow$ $2200 = V_{0} × 10$ $\Rightarrow$ $V_{0} = 220 V$

$\because$ $\frac{V_{i}}{V_{0}}=\frac{N_{P}}{N_{S}}\Rightarrow V_{i}=2\times 220=440V$

Also, $P_{0} = V_{i}I_{i}$

$\Rightarrow I_{i}=\frac{2200}{440}=5A$

text:
A moving coil galvanometer allows a full scale
current of $10^{–4} A. A$ series resistance of 2 M$\Omega$
is required to convert the above galvanometer
into a voltmeter of range 0-5 V. Therefore the
value of shunt resistance required to convert the
above galvanometer into an ammeter of range
0-10 mA is :
options: None of the options are correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given data,

$\begin{array}{l} I=10^{-4}\mathrm{A}, \\  \\ R_{S}=2\mathrm{M}\Omega =2\times 10^{6}\Omega , \\  \\ V_{\max }=5\mathrm{V} \end{array}$

Let internal resistance of galvanometer is $R_{G}$.


[IMG]


Then,

$\begin{array}{l} I\times R_{S}+I\times R_{G}=V_{\max } \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2\times 10^{6}\times 10^{-4}+10^{-4}\times R_{G}=5 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 10^{-4}R_{G}=5-200=-195 \\  \\ \text{or}R_{G}=-195\times 10^{4}\Omega  \end{array}$

Resistance cannot be negative.

$\therefore$ No option is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text:
$A 25 × 10^{–3} m^{3}$ volume cylinder is filled with
1 mol of $O_{2}$ gas at room temperature (300K).
The molecular diameter of $O_{2}$, and its root
mean square speed, are found to be 0.3 nm, and
200 m/s, respectively. What is the average
collision rate (per second) for an $O_{2}$ molecule ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The number density of molecules is

$n=\dfrac{N_{A}}{V}=\dfrac{6.02\times 10^{23}}{25\times 10^{-3}}\approx 2.4\times 10^{25}\text{m}^{-3}.$

The mean free path is

$λ=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}πd^{2}n}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}π\left (0.3\times 10^{-9}\right )^{2}\left (2.4\times 10^{25}\right )}\approx 1.0\times 10^{-7}\text{m}.$

The average collision rate is

$\dfrac{v}{λ}=\dfrac{200}{1.0\times 10^{-7}}\approx 2\times 10^{9}\text{s}^{-1},$

which, among the given orders of magnitude, is closest to $10^{10}\text{s}^{-1}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text:
A uniformly charged ring of radius 3a and total
charge q is placed in xy-plane centred at origin.
A point charge q is moving towards the ring
along the z-axis and has speed u at z = 4a. The
minimum value of u such that it crosses the
origin is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $k=\dfrac{1}{4πε_{0}}$, the potential of the ring (radius $3a$, charge $q$) at a point on its axis at height $z$ is

$V(z)=\frac{kq}{\sqrt{9a^{2}+z^{2}}}$

$V$ is largest at the origin, so the charge crosses the origin if its kinetic energy at $z=4a$ covers the rise in potential energy from $z=4a$ to $z=0$:

$\frac{1}{2}mu^{2}=q[V(0)-V(4a)]=kq^{2}\left (\frac{1}{3a}-\frac{1}{5a}\right )=\frac{2kq^{2}}{15a}$

$u=\sqrt{\frac{2}{m}}\left (\frac{2}{15}\frac{q^{2}}{4πε_{0}a}\right )^{1/2}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot
